Off the wall

W5 · tmux panes

The turn is a terminal split: a tail -f updates pane beside the step log, a vim status line, and keys to jump to #7 or the open Ask.

Builds on
M4 (paging through updates, here a cursor you move with j/k), B7 (steps between updates compress, here into vim folds) and M7's composer. New: the updates stream and the step log are two panes of one window, and moving the cursor to an update scrolls the log to that moment.
Placement
Inside the single activity block, under its head and strip: a fixed-height tmux window with tail -f updates (left, two thirds) and log (right), and a status line along the bottom. Final reply below the block, composer below that.
Live
The updates pane follows the tail: the newest line fades in and a blinking cursor marks follow mode. Moving the cursor stops following; G resumes. The status line carries a pink ? 1 open the whole time.
Settled
The window stays attached on the latest turn. The cursor starts on the open Ask (#26) with the log pane synced to 31:02, not at the bottom. Resolved Blocked lines carry [resolved #13]. The pane ends in (END) turn settled at 44:30.
Collapsible
⏏ on the status line, q, or the activity chevron detaches the window. Only the status line stays: detached · 34 updates · last ✓ Branch pushed…, with ? 1 open still tappable. The latest turn is attached by default and older turns are detached.
Short-session-threads
The window is a fixed 300px on desktop (about 20 lines for the whole block, whatever the count) and 3 lines when detached. On the phone the pane is 316px live and 214px settled, and 3 lines detached. The log is a pane inside the same block, so there is still exactly one activity block.
Easy-to-read
Every update is shown in full, with no clamp, at 12.5px (12px+ on the phone). Each has a hanging line number and an uppercase type tag in its colour with its glyph (? ASK, ✕ BLOCKED). Lower-p updates are in secondary ink. The cost: on a 590px column the split leaves the updates pane about 45 characters wide. z zooms it to full width.
Mobile-friendly
The panes become two full-width tabs you swipe between (scroll-snap), and the status line becomes the tab switcher at thumb height. A Termux-style extra-keys row (? ask · ▲ · ▼ · / find · G end · ⏏) replaces the keyboard. The window has a fixed height, so the final reply and composer never move, and detaching gives the screen back.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
Click the window to focus it (keys only work while it has focus, so it never fights the composer). 7G jumps to update #7, j/k step through, / searches (Enter jumps, n/N cycle), ? cycles Asks then Blocked, open ones first. gg/G jump to the ends, h/l switch panes, +/− change density. The phone gets the same actions from the key row.
Needs-reply
The open Ask carries an inverse awaiting you badge on its line, and the status line shows a pink ? 1 open that jumps to it, even while the window is detached. On settle the cursor starts on it. ? reaches it from anywhere.
Density
The final key bal all buttons on the status line (+/− on the keyboard). Final only detaches every window. Key, Balanced (default) and All hide lower tiers behind vim folds (+-- 3 below level · ● 2 ✓ 1) that stay in place and open on click, so the list never pretends to be short.
At-150
Nothing grows: the pane stays 300px and scrolls. Balanced at 150 is roughly 65 lines plus folds, and the status line reads #87 · 65/150. 87G, / and ? reach anything without scrolling. The log pane is already long (211 lines here), so it doesn't change.
Build-cost
M. The panes and the list are ordinary. The work is key handling scoped to focus, the time sync between update and step (step timestamps already exist), fold grouping, and the phone tab variant.
Trade-off
Nested scroll regions inside a scrolling transcript. The idiom is keyboard-first and pays off mainly for vim and tmux users, and on touch the key row is a crutch. Split panes are narrow on a desktop column. Steal: linked panes, where selecting an update scrolls the step log to that moment, plus 7G and ? as keyboard jumps for any digest.

Off the wall

W6 · Git graph

The turn as git log --graph: every surfaced update is a commit, Decisions fork to the path not taken, Corrections are fixup!s, and the Ask is an open review thread.

Builds on
M1 (a chronological list inside the activity block, with the steps folded under each item) and B3 (typed chips). New: the digest is drawn as git log --graph, newest first, and the relationships between updates are drawn instead of implied: forks, fixups, resolutions.
Placement
Inside the single activity block, below its head and strip: a command bar, then a graph capped at 390px (330px on the phone) that scrolls on its own. The final reply and composer sit below the block, unchanged.
Live
The top row is the working tree: a dashed, rotating node reading Running pnpm acceptance:visual, with the uncommitted step as its diff. Below it, HEAD sits on the newest update (#30). Each new update lands under the working tree and HEAD moves up.
Settled
The working tree row disappears, HEAD also gets origin/feat/typed-session-list, and the graph opens scrolled to the open review thread (#26), not to the top. Milestones carry tags (tag: sidebar-typed) that work as section markers.
Collapsible
Click the activity head, or -1, to collapse to two lines: HEAD's oneline with 34 commits, and the open thread in pink. Each line jumps back into the graph. On the phone, settled opens collapsed so the reply is on screen.
Short-session-threads
The graph never grows past 390px (about 9 updates in view), and collapsed it is two lines. Below-level updates squash into one dotted row: 3 squashed · ● 2 ✓ 1 · show. There is one activity block. The log lives inside each commit's diff, not in a second block.
Easy-to-read
Every update is shown in full at 13px, with a typed chip, #n and time on a header line above it. Invented one-liners are in secondary ink. Node shape reinforces type: square for Blocked, solid pink with ? for the Ask. Hashes are gold and quiet. The cost is density: the header line doubles the height of each update compared with a plain list.
Mobile-friendly
The lane narrows to 28px and hashes and remotes are hidden. Every string is 12px or larger, and headers wrap instead of truncating. The command bar wraps to two rows. Thread answers are 32px-tall buttons. Settled opens collapsed (two lines) so the reply and composer own the screen.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
show # jumps to any update (type 7 and press Enter), expanding squashed rows as needed. fixup! #2, ↶ corrected by #14 and ✓ resolved by #13 are links. With the graph focused, j/k move, Enter or o opens a commit's diff (its tool steps with timestamps), and t jumps to the thread.
Needs-reply
The Ask is a GitHub-style review thread · open box with Recapture / Keep old order / Reply… right in the graph. A pink ? 1 open thread ref in the command bar jumps to it, and the collapsed form keeps it as its own pink line. Answering resolves the thread in place.
Density
The flags are the density control: -1 (Final only: collapsed), --key, --balanced (default) and --all. Below-level updates become squash rows with per-type counts, so the list never pretends to be short. HEAD, the working tree and the root are always pinned.
At-150
The cap holds, and at Balanced about 60 updates remain, broken up by squash rows. Tags on milestones give landmarks, and show # handles the rest. The weakness: with no search, long mid-turn stretches are reached only by scrolling or by number.
Build-cost
M. A single-lane graph is CSS (a border and a node), and forks are one SVG per alternative. The real cost is data: "not taken" alternatives and fixup or resolved links need the agent (or Jev) to emit those relations. Without them the design falls back to M1 with nodes.
Trade-off
The metaphor is borrowed, not native. Non-git users see hashes and refs as noise, and the relations it draws well need structured data the pipeline doesn't yet produce. The header line costs height. Steal: show a Decision together with the option not taken, and link updates to each other (fixup! #2, resolved by #13) instead of leaving the reader to connect them.

Off the wall

W7 · Binder tabs

The activity block is a ring binder: one surfaced update per fixed-height page, typed index tabs down its edge, and the open Ask's tab sticking out.

Builds on
M4 (one update at a time with a pager) and B3 (typed colour and glyph). New: the index of pages is a row of physical tabs on the block's edge, so the shape of the turn (how many Decisions, where the Ask is) is visible without reading anything.
Placement
The single activity block becomes a ring binder: punched holes and a margin rule on the left, one fixed-height page per surfaced update, and index tabs sticking out of the right edge on desktop, or hanging off the bottom edge on the phone. Final reply and composer below.
Live
The binder opens on the newest page (#30, marked newest). New updates add a tab at the bottom of the index. Reading an older page doesn't get interrupted: the tab appears, and the page stays put. The open Ask tab sticks out further and glows pink.
Settled
The binder opens on the open Ask (p26) with its two answers on the page. The final reply is below the binder, always visible. The back of the binder is the step log (a ≡ log tab), with 211 lines scrolling inside the page.
Collapsible
Clicking the chevron or head shuts the binder to its head plus one row of coloured glyph nubs (one per in-level page) and ? open · p26. Each nub opens the binder at that page. final shuts it too. Older turns are shut by default.
Short-session-threads
The page is a fixed height (190px desktop, 212px phone), so the block is about 270px whether there are 3 updates or 150, and about 60px when shut. Exactly one activity block: the log is the binder's back page, not a second block.
Easy-to-read
One update per page at 14px (13.5px phone), with room for the whole sentence and nothing competing with it. The kicker shows the type in a boxed glyph and colour, the time and p, and Decision 3 of 6 · p20 for orientation. A dashed trail line gives the steps leading up to it (4 steps before this · last: Ran pnpm check). Stand-ins are marked and in secondary ink.
Mobile-friendly
Tabs move to the bottom edge, grouped by type (? 1 · ✕ 2 · ! 2 · ◆ 6…), each 30px tall and full-width in total. The Ask tab is 38px and glows. Swipe the page left and right to flip, and tap a group again to go back through older pages of that type. Every string is 12px+ and the fixed page height means the reply never moves.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
Type a page number into the footer (7 and Enter) to jump there directly. Tabs jump in one click, and hovering a tab on desktop peeks at its text. With the page focused, ←/→ flip, ? opens the Ask, and Home/End go to the first and last pages. Links on pages (✓ resolved on p13, ↶ corrects p2) cross-reference. Weakness: you read one page at a time, so there is no scanning several at once.
Needs-reply
The Ask tab protrudes further than the others and pulses pink at any density. The footer and shut state carry ? open · p26. The page itself has an awaiting you flag with Recapture / Keep old order buttons, and answering calms the tab.
Density
final key bal all in the footer. The level decides which pages get tabs and which pages ◀▶ flip through. Below-level pages stay reachable by number, so nothing is lost. Final only shuts the binder. When the tabs no longer fit (All, 34 pages), the index regroups by type automatically, with a count on each tab.
At-150
The block's height doesn't change. Tabs regroup by type (at most 9 plus the log), each group cycles newest to oldest, and the page number field reaches any of the 150. The open Ask still protrudes. The weakness: finding a particular Finding among 60 means tapping one group many times, with no search.
Build-cost
S–M. Pages, tabs and the pager are plain components with one bit of state. Swipe uses pointer events. Tab fitting and grouping is a single measurement. The binder chrome is two background gradients and a pseudo-element.
Trade-off
You see exactly one update at a time, so reading the whole story is 15 flips instead of one scroll, and skimming suffers most. The desktop tabs need 46px of right gutter. Steal: give the digest a fixed height, one message per page, with a typed index on the block's edge and a protruding tab for the open Ask, so the shape of the turn and the pending question are visible at a glance.
